subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does a controlled current-main raw-WebSocket test show that a guessed event `seq` can make an unauthenticated or different connection inject a request or receive another connection's events?
rationale: Protected security labels require explicit owner disposition, and only a boundary test can resolve the remaining possibility of a dispatch flaw not visible in the reported code argument.

options.title: Verify and close
options.body: Run the cross-connection boundary test and close the report if authentication, scopes, and socket ownership reject every guessed-sequence attempt.

options.title: Escalate privately
options.body: If the test demonstrates cross-connection acceptance or unauthorized event access, move the concrete reproduction into a private GitHub Security Advisory and repair the actual dispatch boundary.

recommendation.title: Verify and close
recommendation.body: Run the cross-connection boundary test and close the report if authentication, scopes, and socket ownership reject every guessed-sequence attempt.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history most directly covers gateway WebSocket scope, pairing, and authorization hardening on the alleged boundary.
